block.trackssimulate.track_mount.tooltip: _Attaches_ suspension tracks or drive wheels to the mount.
_Transfers_ drive from powered track drive wheels into connected track segments.
_Hides_ the mount or visual suspension depending on the clicked face.
When Sneak R-Clicked with a Wrench
Mounts _track-like_ items to allow for tracked ground travel.
item.trackssimulate.suspension_key.toolt: _Cycles_ the selected tuning mode. Sneaking cycles backward.
_Tunes_ the selected suspension setting for connected tracks or wheels.
_Moves_ the track or wheel position from the clicked face.
_Resets_ suspension tuning while keeping position offsets.
Tunes _track and wheel suspension_ across connected mounts.
screen.trackssimulate.hint: Physical tuning is shared; position edits have a selectable scope.
setting.trackssimulate.strength.tooltip: Controls each road wheel's base spring stiffness, not vehicle mass in kilograms. It combines with the spring multiplier. Raising it reduces compression under a given load; lowering it makes the suspension softer. Integer values only. Drive wheels remain fixed and do not gain suspension support.
setting.trackssimulate.spring.tooltip: Multiplies spring stiffness on top of load strength. A larger value resists compression more strongly; a smaller value permits more compression under the same load. It does not change wheel size or suspension travel. Tune load strength first, then use this for finer adjustment.
setting.trackssimulate.damping.tooltip: Scales resistance to relative suspension motion using the supported mass and spring stiffness. It controls how compression and rebound settle, not the static ride height or maximum travel. High values can slow the response. For heavy-vehicle tests, change only this setting between runs and retain the physics logs.
setting.trackssimulate.bump_clearance.to: Progressive spring onset multiplier near compression end. Onset relative to the offset point is E-C+min(0.15*value,C*0.9). Higher values start earlier without changing travel limits. The bump spring shares the spring cap; the hard stop is independent.
setting.trackssimulate.bump_force.toolti: Additional progressive spring stiffness near compression end. Subject to the spring impulse cap; the independent compression stop is not limited by that cap.
setting.trackssimulate.max_impulse.toolt: Per-wheel spring impulse cap multiplier, based on supported mass and timestep. Limits main and progressive springs only; the compression stop has an independent unilateral solve. Low values may allow bottoming, but do not suppress stop support. Inspect springCapSteps, stopImpulseSum and penetrationMax.
setting.trackssimulate.drive.tooltip: Scales the propulsion force generated from the connected drive input. A larger value increases available driving force, subject to contact and friction limits. It does not multiply the input RPM or set a target track speed. Without drive input this setting does not create power.
setting.trackssimulate.grip.tooltip: Increases both lateral resistance and the contact friction budget. It needs a positive support impulse to provide traction. A larger value resists sideways sliding but can also make skid steering harder. It is not a wheel-width setting or an independent longitudinal friction control.
setting.trackssimulate.lateral.tooltip: Moves along the local track direction, clockwise from the block facing. Applies to both drive and road wheels with the selected scope. Wheel centers and belt attachments move; block and shaft interfaces stay in place. Drive wheels remain unsprung. Angled belt spans between independently offset wheels are retained.
setting.trackssimulate.longitudinal.tool: Moves along the axle in the block facing direction; this does not change wheel width. Applies to both drive and road wheels with the selected scope. Wheel centers and belt attachments move; block and shaft interfaces stay in place. Drive wheels remain unsprung. Angled belt spans between independently offset wheels are retained.
setting.trackssimulate.height.tooltip:
Moves vertically in the chassis local frame; this is not suspension travel. Applies to both drive and road wheels with the selected scope. Wheel centers and belt attachments move; block and shaft interfaces stay in place. Drive wheels remain unsprung. Angled belt spans between independently offset wheels are retained.
For road wheels, downward offset D=-Height. Compression must not exceed D+Extension. Use Sync to submit dependent changes together.
screen.trackssimulate.editor_hint: Enter/Apply sends one field; Push sends all; selected scope applies to every action.
screen.trackssimulate.input.tooltip: Enter/Apply submits this field. ± adjusts the typed value and submits immediately. Yellow/* = unsubmitted; red = invalid. Esc/Done discards unsubmitted edits. Scroll when space is limited.
screen.trackssimulate.timeout: %s: no confirmation; current server value %s. Check distance/permission and retry.
screen.trackssimulate.reset.sent: Physics reset requested; dimensions and offsets preserved.
screen.trackssimulate.reset.tooltip: Reset physics tuning in the selected scope; keep geometry and visibility.
screen.trackssimulate.hide.tooltip: Toggles the suspension strut on this wheel only. It does not hide the wheel or disable physics.
screen.trackssimulate.done.tooltip: Closes the editor. Submitted settings remain; unfinished input is discarded. Use Enter or Apply first to save a typed value.
screen.trackssimulate.offset_scope.toolt: All operations use this scope. Linked same-role sync stays within the belt. Unlinked same-role sync searches loaded, unlinked wheels on the same Sable body within 8 blocks (maximum 64); never loads chunks. Whole belt requires a connection. Unsupported fields are skipped.
screen.trackssimulate.sync_group.tooltip: Push all valid editor values, including drafts, to the selected scope. Never pulls from neighbors. Invalid geometry rejects the whole submission and retains drafts.
setting.trackssimulate.width.tooltip: Centered on the axle; 1 is one block wide. Uses the selected scope. Belt width interpolates between wheels. Linking does not overwrite widths.
setting.trackssimulate.scale.tooltip: Multiplier of this wheel type's default diameter. 2 doubles the diameter without moving the center. Group sync uses each wheel's own base size. Existing saved radii are preserved.
setting.trackssimulate.hidden.tooltip: Road wheels only: 1 hides the strut, 0 shows it. Physics stays active. Other roles skip this field.
setting.trackssimulate.wheel_hidden.tool: 1 hides the wheel mesh only. Belt, path, support and drive remain active. The suspension strut has its own setting. Applies to all wheel roles in the selected scope.
setting.trackssimulate.through_axle.tool: 0 = left half (mount/back face); 1 = full (both faces); 2 = right half (wheel/front face); 3 = no axle (neither external input nor output). These labels follow block facing, not world east/west. This changes kinetic ports only, not models or fixed collision. Drive wheels in the same belt share Create kinetics at a 1:1 shaft ratio, including stress and conflict handling. No-axle wheels still follow the belt but cannot supply external shafts. Wheel size and belt speed gain do not change the 1:1 shaft ratio.
setting.trackssimulate.speed.tooltip: Drive wheels only. Multiplies input RPM for belt drive, independently of drive force gain and shaft output. Existing radius/winding ratios still apply. The first powered drive in selection order supplies the loop; multipliers do not stack. This is a speed gain in the existing drive backend, not a power-conserving gearbox simulation.
setting.trackssimulate.max_extension.too: Downward extension E measured from the configured offset point. With downward offset D=-Height, full droop is D+E below the original anchor. No support beyond droop. Compression C shortens from full droop; absolute downward travel is [D+E-C, D+E]. Default E: 0.60/0.75/0.95. Edit dependent fields together and use Sync to submit atomically.
setting.trackssimulate.max_compression.t: Maximum shortening C from full extension, not an upward mount coordinate. C may exceed E but must satisfy 0<=C<=D+E, where D=-Height. Example: Height=-0.5, E=0.8, C=1.0 gives downward positions 0.3..1.3. C=0 gives zero stroke. An independent compression stop supports the chassis beyond the spring impulse budget. Finite timesteps and terrain sampling can still produce transient overlap; this is not full wheel/belt collision. Invalid batches are rejected.
setting.trackssimulate.contact_spread.to: Scales the spacing of the fixed five rays along and across the wheel. 1 preserves the original footprint; 1.25 reaches the width edges. Longitudinal samples follow the circular underside. No extra rays or larger model. This is road-wheel sampling, not full-belt or side collision (M3).
setting.trackssimulate.contact_margin.to: Extra query distance above the compression end and beyond full droop. Detects contact transitions and out-of-travel surfaces without changing wheel size or suspension travel. A detected surface beyond maximum extension never supplies support. Does not add rays.
Friction along the belt. Higher values allow stronger traction and braking when friction-limited, without increasing cruise damping. Full redstone braking solves for zero contact speed within the friction budget. Zero disables longitudinal track traction, drag and braking impulses. With both friction axes zero, tracks provide no grip; other collisions or Sable damping may still slow the vehicle.
setting.trackssimulate.friction_side.too: Friction across the belt. Higher values resist turning and sideways slope slip. Zero completely disables lateral track friction impulses. Both axes share an elliptical budget based on terrain, grip gain and actual normal support.
